findings.title: Build staleness defense is procedural, not structural: nothing in the edit->commit->sync chain ever runs `npm run build`; precommit guard only checks a dist .mjs was co-staged, with no src->dist content link
findings.observe_how: Edit a hook .ts, run `npm run build` to regen ALL dist (esbuild bundles shared/*.ts into every entrypoint), but `git add` only ONE unrelated dist .mjs alongside the .ts -> precommit-build-guard passes (exit 0) -> forward-sync copies the STALE .mjs of the actually-edited hook into ~/.claude/hooks/dist/ -> active hook runs old code. Reproduce by staging src+a stale/unrelated dist and confirming the guard allows it.
findings.telemetry: Add a build-stamp manifest: build writes sha256 of every src/*.ts into dist/.build-manifest.json; the precommit guard recomputes and compares. A drift = block. Today nothing detects 'staged .mjs does not correspond to staged .ts'.

evidence.quote:

findings.title: Post-commit forward-sync runs detached in the background with NO lock; nothing waits for it -> dist-staleness window: active ~/.claude/hooks/dist/*.mjs can lag the just-committed repo dist for the sync's duration, and concurrent commits race the same cp targets
findings.observe_how: Two terminals each `git commit` a hook change within the same ~few-second window (each sync cp-loops hundreds of files with no mutex). Both run `sync-to-active.sh` concurrently writing the SAME ~/.claude/hooks/dist/*.mjs and ~/.claude/settings.json (jq merge via mktemp+mv). Observe interleaved/torn writes. Also: a hook firing in any session DURING the background sync reads a half-copied dist dir.
findings.telemetry: Wrap the cp+verify body of sync-to-active.sh in an flock (or mkdir-based lock) on ~/.claude/.sync.lock so overlapping forward-syncs serialize; emit a 'sync_skipped_locked' / 'sync_overlap' counter to confirm how often concurrency actually occurs in multi-terminal use.

findings.title: The only dist-staleness detector (session-start-init-check) is advisory-only, fires at NEXT SessionStart, checks the wrong target (repo dist DIR-mtime, never active ~/.claude dist), and uses a coarse dir-mtime comparison that an in-place cp can defeat on Windows
findings.observe_how: Read the freshness block: it gates on `projectDir.includes('continuous-claude')` and stats `.claude/hooks/dist` (the REPO dir), comparing each src .ts mtime to the dist DIRECTORY mtime. It never inspects ~/.claude/hooks/dist (what actually runs). It only pushes a `maintenanceWarnings` string; it never blocks and never rebuilds. So a stale dist that ran the entire session surfaces only as text at the next session start, in the repo project only.
findings.telemetry: Compare per-file: for each src X.ts, stat the corresponding dist X.mjs (not the dir); and run the check against ACTIVE ~/.claude/hooks/dist, not the repo. Better: a SessionStart that rebuilds-or-blocks rather than printing a warning the model may ignore.

findings.title: architecture-stats-sync fires a DETACHED background `sync-architecture-stats.mjs --apply` on every watched commit, rewriting tracked architecture.json AFTER the commit -> perpetual post-commit working-tree dirt (the `M architecture.json` in this session's git status)
findings.observe_how: Hook is PostToolUse:Bash; on a commit touching .claude/{hooks,agents,skills}/ or scripts/ it spawns detached `node scripts/sync-architecture-stats.mjs --apply` which writes docs/architecture/system-visualization/architecture.json. Because it runs AFTER the commit, the regenerated file is left uncommitted. The review's own session `git status` opened with `M docs/architecture/system-visualization/architecture.json`; architecture-stats-sync.log confirms it fired ('done: stats synced.').
findings.telemetry: Count how often `git status` is non-clean solely due to architecture.json after a commit. Either (a) make the sync part of pre-commit so it lands in the same commit, or (b) gitignore the generated artifact and regenerate on demand.

evidence.quote:

 * `scripts/sync-architecture-stats.mjs --apply` in the background
 * (fire-and-forget; never blocks the user).

findings.title: architecture-stats-sync is registered in ACTIVE ~/.claude/settings.json but NOT in repo .claude/settings.json -> a new machine bootstrapping from the repo template silently loses this commit-chain hook (same class as SEED-15)
findings.observe_how: Grep both settings.json: repo's has no architecture-stats-sync entry; active ~/.claude/settings.json registers `node ~/.claude/hooks/dist/architecture-stats-sync.mjs` on PostToolUse:Bash (and it has fired -- 55KB log). Per sync-known-gaps.md settings.json is intentionally NOT synced, so the repo template is the new-machine source of truth and it omits this hook. The hook .ts + dist .mjs exist in the repo (dead until hand-registered).
findings.telemetry: Reconcile the active vs repo settings.json hook registration sets; the delta IS the new-machine gap. This is the same root cause SEED-15 found for package-install-guard et al.

findings.title: On a single `git commit` of a hook edit, THREE write-side actors fire with no ordering/exclusion: background forward-sync (active dir), git-commit-roadmap (non-atomic RMW of ROADMAP.md), architecture-stats-sync (detached writer of architecture.json) -- each a separate unguarded fs.writeFileSync/cp into a shared file
findings.observe_how: git-commit-roadmap does fs.readFileSync(ROADMAP) then fs.writeFileSync(ROADMAP) with no lock; under two concurrent commits (multi-terminal, both editing the same repo) the second clobbers the first's roadmap append. This is the same single-writer-violation class as SEED-02's roadmap contamination. The three actors write disjoint files this run, so no direct corruption today, but the pattern (full-file RMW, no lock, fire-on-every-commit) is the recurrence vector the May-2026 history warns about.
findings.telemetry: Wrap ROADMAP.md and architecture.json writes in the same lock the forward-sync needs (D10b-02). Track concurrent-commit collisions via a write-attempt log keyed by file+pid.

findings.title: git-auto-commit (PostToolUse:Write|Edit) does `git add -A` over ALL of ~/.claude including dist files the background forward-sync is concurrently overwriting -> can snapshot a half-synced active dist into a safety commit
findings.observe_how: git-auto-commit only acts when the edited file is under ~/.claude (isInClaudeDir) -- so it is NOT in the repo-edit path -- but when a DIRECT ~/.claude edit triggers it, doCommit runs `git add -A` (stages everything in ~/.claude). If a forward-sync from a concurrent repo commit is mid-flight, the -A stages a partially-copied dist tree. Debounced to 10min so the window is narrow, but the `add -A` blast radius is wider than the file that triggered it. Payoff: scoping the add to the triggering path (or the debounce key) avoids snapshotting unrelated in-flight sync state.
findings.telemetry: Replace `git add -A` with staging only tracked changes relevant to the edit, or guard with the same sync lock (D10b-02).

May-2026 regression defense structural-vs-procedural: VERIFIED -- reverse-sync now guarded (set -e + uncommitted-abort, procedural) but FORWARD sync on every commit has ZERO concurrency control; the build step is fully procedural (manual npm run build, no auto-build anywhere). Net: defense is PROCEDURAL, not structural (D10b-01/02/03 substantiate).
notes:
Slice = D10b end-to-end edit-hook->commit chain (build/sync races, double-writes, ordering, May-2026 regression structural-vs-procedural). Bottom line: the May-2026 regression class is defended PROCEDURALLY, not structurally. The build itself is never automated anywhere in the chain (npm run build is manual; both git-hooks and sync-to-active.sh deliberately skip it because it hangs on Windows); the precommit guard only checks that SOME dist .mjs was co-staged with no src->dist content link (D10b-01); the forward-sync that propagates dist to the live ~/.claude runs detached in the background with no lock and nothing waits for it (D10b-02); and the sole staleness detector is an advisory SessionStart string that checks the wrong (repo, not active) dist dir with a coarse dir-mtime comparison (D10b-03). Reverse-sync was hardened after May-2026, but forward-sync -- the direction that actually ships code to the running hooks -- was not.

Cross-links to seeds: D10b-05 is the same root cause as SEED-15 (settings.json not synced -> new-machine registration gaps); D10b-06 is the same single-writer/non-atomic-RMW class as SEED-02 (roadmap contamination). D10b-04 (architecture.json post-commit dirt) directly explains the `M docs/architecture/system-visualization/architecture.json` present in this review session's opening git status.

Not re-discovered (out of slice, already covered by prior dims): post-edit-diagnostics tsc 30s blocking spawn and bus mutateBus 200ms-cap behavior are noted as VERIFIED-benign in the coverage manifest, not raised as findings.
